Puhun is called Shelun's junior paternal uncle, which entails an unnamed father of Shelun. No year is given.
Puhun is Shelun's father's younger brother and the father of Datan. No year is given.
Chiluohou had helped Shelun earlier. Buluzhen later drove him to suicide. No year is given.

claims.statement: Besieged by Buluzhen, Chiluohou burned his treasures and cut his own throat.

claims.event: Chiluohou's young wife told Buluzhen of the plan to raise Datan. No year is given.

claims.statement: Chiluohou means to make Datan chief and has sent him a golden bridle as a pledge.

claims.event: Sheba, Shelun's son, was strangled by Datan together with Buluzhen. No year is given.

claims.statement: Datan captured Sheba with Buluzhen and strangled him.

claims.event: In autumn of Shiguang 1, after Mingyuan's death, Datan attacked Yunzhong and besieged Taiwu.
In year 2 of the Shiguang campaign Datan's people fled north.
In the eighth month of Shenjia 1 Datan sent a son with ten thousand horse across the border.
In year 2, after Shenjia 1, Datan's host fled west from the Li River and he vanished.

claims.statement: Datan captured Buluzhen and Sheba and strangled them, then set himself up.

claims.event: Hulu's son reached Helong with him and Feng Ba enfeoffed them, in the Shenrui 1 episode.
Emperor Mingyuan campaigned against Datan and later died, before the autumn of Shiguang 1.

claims.statement: Emperor Mingyuan died. Taiwu succeeded, and in the autumn of Shiguang 1 Datan attacked Yunzhong.

claims.event: In year 2 Xi Jin, Prince of Yicheng, took the western route from Erhan Mountain.
Earlier, as Marquis of Shanyang, Xi Jin pursued Datan in the snow. That pursuit has no numbered year.
Taiwu had taken the throne when, in autumn of Shiguang 1, he reached Yunzhong and was besieged by Datan.
In year 2 Taiwu advanced in five columns against Datan.
In year 2 after Shenjia 1 Taiwu marched to the Li River and on to the Tuyuan River.

claims.statement: Liu Yilong can barely save himself. If the Rouran are not crushed first, Wei would be caught between two enemies. He will go.

claims.event: Earlier Dana, Datan's brother, lost a contest with Shelun and fled to Wei. That earlier flight has no year here.
During the Shiguang 1 fighting, Wei soldiers shot and killed Yuzhijin, Dana's son, whom Datan had made a chief.

claims.statement: Wei soldiers shot and killed Yuzhijin during the Shiguang 1 campaign.

claims.event: In year 2 Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, advanced from the Black Desert.
In the fifth month of the Shenjia 2 campaign Changsun Han struck Pili and killed hundreds of their chiefs.
In year 2 Changsun Daosheng, Duke of Ruyin, advanced between the White and Black Deserts.
In year 2 E Qing, Duke of Dongping, advanced on the west from Suyuan.
In year 2 General Anyuan took the western route from Erhan Mountain.
In the eighth month of the Shenjia 2 campaign Taiwu sent Anyuan, left vice director, against the Gaoche at Sini Po.
In the eighth month of Shenjia 1 Datan's son led more than ten thousand horse across the border, plundered, and escaped.
In the fourth month of year 2, Zhang Yuan cited astronomy to stop Taiwu's attack on Datan.
In the fourth month of year 2, Xu Bian cited astronomy to stop Taiwu's attack on Datan.
In year 2 Taiwu rejected the diviners and followed Cui Hao's plan to march.
During year 2, envoys reported that Liu Yilong meant to attack Henan and demanded the land back.

claims.statement: Return our Henan lands and the army will stand down; otherwise he will use his full strength.

claims.event: In the Shenjia 2 campaign Pili, Datan's younger brother, marched to join him and was struck by Changsun Han.
Taiwu passed the old fort of the Han general Dou Xian. The text gives no year for Dou Xian himself.
Datan's tribe had weakened and he died of illness. No year is written on the death.

claims.statement: Datan died of illness, and his son Wuti succeeded.

claims.event: In year 4, before Yanhe 3, Wuti sent tribute. The year is read as Shenjia 4.
In the second month of Yanhe 3 Wuti married the Princess of Xihai and sent his brother Tuluigui to court.
In Taiyan 2 Wuti broke the peace and raided the border.
In year 5, after Taiyan, Wuti raided while Taiwu attacked Juqu Mujian.
In Zhenjun 4 Wuti fled from the Ergen River.
In year 5 after Zhenjun 4 Wuti fled a planned ambush.

claims.statement: Wuti died and his son Tuhezhen succeeded. The death sentence gives no year.

claims.event: In Yanhe 3 Taiwu sent envoys to take Wuti's sister as consort and rewarded Tuluigui.
In year 4 after Taiyan 2 the emperor went to Wuyuan and campaigned.
In year 5 the emperor marched west against Juqu Mujian.
In Zhenjun 4 the emperor campaigned to the Ergen River.
In the first month of year 10, read as Zhenjun 10, the emperor marched north with Jingmu.
In the second month of Yanhe 3 the Princess of Xihai was married to Wuti.
In Yanhe 3 Wei took Wuti's younger sister as consort and later advanced her to Left Brilliant Consort.
In Yanhe 3 Wuti's elder brother Tuluigui came to court with two thousand horses.
In year 4 Pi, Prince of Leping, led fifteen generals on the eastern route.
In year 4 Heduoluo, Duke of Hedong, went east with Pi.
In year 4 Jian, Prince of Yongchang, led the western route. The English surname Wang is not in 永昌王健.
In year 5 Mu Shou, Prince of Yidu, stayed to aid Jingmu and failed to prepare for Wuti.
In the year-4 campaign Chong, Prince of Chenliu, marched from the Great Marsh toward Zhuoye Mountain.
In year 5 the emperor marched west against Juqu Mujian.
In year 5 Mu Shou aided Jingmu in holding the capital.
In the first month of year 10 Jingmu went north with the emperor by the middle route.
In year 5 Ji Jing, Prince of Changle, held the southern desert and later captured Qiliegui.
In year 5 Chong, Prince of Jianning, held the southern desert with Ji Jing.
In Zhenjun 4 Chong, Prince of Jianning, led fifteen generals on the east.
In the year-5 invasion Wuti's elder brother Qiliegui was captured north of Yin Mountain.

claims.statement: The Juqu have undone me.

claims.event: In the year-5 fighting the Wei captured Tawuwuluhu, called the paternal elder uncle, and five hundred commanders.
In the year-5 raid Changsun Daosheng, minister of works, held Mount Tuhui and pursued Wuti to the southern desert.
In Zhenjun 4 the Prince of Leping, personal name not repeated, led fifteen generals on the west.
In Zhenjun 4 Fan, Prince of Le'an, led fifteen generals on the east.
In Zhenjun 4 Chen, Prince of Zhongshan, led the central reserve.
In year 10, read as Zhenjun 10, Tuhezhen was newly enthroned and fled the northern campaign.
In Tai'an 4 Tuhezhen fled a northern campaign and his minister Wuzhu Jiatui surrendered.
In Heping 5 Tuhezhen died and his son Yucheng succeeded.

claims.statement: Tuhezhen died in Heping 5.

claims.event: In Tai'an 4 the unnamed emperor marched north across the Gobi. The era is not Taiwu's.
In year 10 Na, Prince of Gaoliang, took the east, held out against Tuhezhen, and pursued him.
In year 10 Jie'er, Prince of Lueyang, campaigned and took more than a million people and animals.
In the year-10 campaign Ermiantaba, a subordinate chief of Tuhezhen, surrendered with a thousand households.
In Tai'an 4 Wuzhu Jiatui, Tuhezhen's mofu, surrendered with several thousand tents.
In Heping 5 Yucheng succeeded Tuhezhen and proclaimed his own Yongkang year 1.
In Huangxing 4 Yucheng raided and Xianzu marched north against him.
In Huangxing 4 Emperor Xianzu swore the army on the Nü River and routed Yucheng.

claims.statement: Victory lies in surprise, not numbers. The generals are to fight their utmost; the plan is already set.

claims.event: In Huangxing 4 Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao, led the western wing.
In Huangxing 4 Yuan Pi, Duke of Dongyang, went west with Zitui. The English calls him a prince; the Chinese says 公.
In Huangxing 4 Yun, Prince of Rencheng, led the east.
In Huangxing 4 Ci, Prince of Ruyin, was in the van. The English Runan is a mistake for Ruyin.
In Huangxing 4 Luo Wuba, Duke of Jinan, was in the van.
In Huangxing 4 Yuan He, Prince of Longxi, commanded the rear.
In Yanxing 5 Yucheng asked for a marriage and Xianzu did not grant it.
In Taihe 9 Yucheng died and his son Douluon succeeded.

claims.statement: Yucheng died in Taihe 9.

claims.event: In Yanxing 5 Emperor Xianzu refused to break off Yucheng's marriage overture.

claims.statement: The Rouran are greedy, but he will treat them with good faith. The marriage has only just been raised and is not yet fitting. A first marriage must honor the rites.

claims.event: In the fourth month of Taihe 1 Biba, titled Mohequfen, brought horses and sable and viewed the capital's treasures.
In the second month of the following year Biba returned with tribute and renewed the marriage request.

claims.statement: The great realm is rich beyond anything they have seen.

claims.event: In Taihe 2 Emperor Xiaowen consented to the Rouran marriage.
In the eighth month of Taihe 16 Xiaowen sent Yi, Lu Rui, and Hulu Huan against Douluon.
In Taihe 9 Douluon succeeded Yucheng and proclaimed his own Taiping year 1.
In the Taihe 16 narrative Douluon was repeatedly defeated by Avozhiluo and then killed with his mother.

claims.statement: The tribes killed Douluon and his mother and showed the bodies to Nagai.
The annal writes Fugudun. The collation says Cefu yuangui and Zizhi tongjian, following Wei Shou as cited by Hu Sansheng, read Fumindun.

claims.event: The collation cites Wei Shou for the reading Fumindun. No year is given for him.
Hu Sansheng is cited for the Fumindun reading. No year is given.
Hou Yiai advised Douluon to keep peace. No year is given.
Douluon accused Shiluohou of treason and killed him, extinguishing three degrees of kin. No year is given.

claims.statement: Douluon executed Shiluohou and exterminated three degrees of his kin.

claims.event: In the eighth month of Taihe 16 Yi, Prince of Yangping, was sent as a commander against Douluon.
In Taihe 16 Lu Rui, left vice director, was joint commander against Douluon.
In Taihe 16 Hulu Huan led part of the seventy thousand cavalry against Douluon.
In the Taihe 16 narrative Avozhiluo led the Gaoche west, proclaimed himself ruler, and defeated Douluon.
In the Taihe 16 narrative Nagai, Douluon's uncle, accepted the throne after Douluon was killed and proclaimed his own Tai'an year 1.
Nagai was dead before Futu's embassy of Zhengshi 3, when Futu was already khan.

claims.statement: He is a subject and cannot become khan.
Nagai died and his son Futu succeeded. The death is before Futu's Zhengshi 3 embassy.

claims.event: Douluon's mother was killed with him in the Taihe 16 narrative.

claims.statement: The tribes killed Douluon's mother together with Douluon.

claims.event: In Zhengshi 3 Futu sent Hexi Wuliuoba to seek peace.
In Yongping 1 Futu again sent Wuliuoba, and Xuanwu refused him.
Futu was killed by Mietuo of the Gaoche before Chounu's embassy of Yongping 4.

claims.statement: Futu campaigned west against the Gaoche and was killed by their king Mietuo.

claims.event: Early in Zhenguang, Shifa killed Anagui's mother, Lady Hou Luling. The English dates the start of Zhenguang to 520.

claims.statement: Shifa killed Anagui's mother, Lady Hou of the Lüling clan, and two of Anagui's younger brothers.
The annal writes Hou of the Lüling clan. A note says Tongzhi and the Gaoche record read Yi or Si, and that Hou is likely corrupt.

claims.event: In Zhengshi 3 Wuliuoba, also called Hexi Wuliuoba, brought Futu's peace request.
In Yongping 1 Wuliuoba brought a letter and sable and was dismissed.
In the year after Xiping 1 Wuliuoba came again with Weibijian and Gong Guli.
In Zhengshi 3 Emperor Xuanwu refused Futu's embassy and lectured Wuliuoba.
In Yongping 1 Xuanwu again refused Wuliuoba.
In the winter of Yanchang 3 Xuanwu appointed Ma Yishu envoy to Chounu but died before he set out. Yanchang 3 is 514, not the English 512; the winter may enter 515.

claims.statement: Emperor Xuanwu died in the winter of Yanchang 3, before Ma Yishu departed.
Shelun, the Rouran ancestor, was a rebel against Wei. Wei's power is rising. Because the south is not yet conquered, a general peace is refused. If they resume vassal rites, they will be rewarded.

claims.event: Xuanwu calls Shelun the distant Rouran ancestor and a rebel. That edict does not date Shelun's life.
In Xiping 1 Chounu captured and killed Mietuo, king of the Gaoche.

claims.statement: Chounu seized Mietuo and killed him in Xiping 1.

claims.event: In the ninth month of Yongping 4 Chounu sent the monk Hong Xuan with a pearl image.
In Xiping 1 Chounu defeated the Gaoche and killed Mietuo.
Early in Zhenguang Chounu was killed by his mother and the ministers after a defeat by Azhiluo.

claims.statement: After his return, Chounu's mother and the chief ministers killed him and set up Anagui.

claims.event: In the ninth month of Yongping 4 the monk Hong Xuan brought a jeweled Buddha image from Chounu.
In the winter of Yanchang 3 Ma Yishu was named envoy to Chounu but never departed because Xuanwu died.
In year 4, after Yanchang 3, Weibijian, titled yijin, brought tribute.
In the year after Xiping 1 Weibijian came again.
In the year after Xiping 1 Gong Guli came with tribute.
In the second month of Shengui 1 Gong Guli was received at Xianyang Hall and admonished.
In the second month of Shengui 1 Emperor Suzong received the Rouran envoys and had Xu He read an edict.
In Shengui 1 Xu He read the edict faulting the Rouran envoys.
Early in Zhenguang Anagui was set up after Chounu's death, defeated by Shifa, and fled south to Wei.
Zuhui was hidden by Diwan and later secretly killed before she herself was killed early in Zhenguang.

claims.statement: Chounu secretly killed Zuhui after Diwan denounced him.
He had stayed in Diwan's house and had not gone to Heaven. Heaven was her teaching.

claims.event: Zuhui's mother exposed Diwan's fraud to Chounu. No year and no personal name.

claims.statement: Diwan was about twenty (年二十許) when, as a healer-shaman, she claimed she could recall Zuhui from Heaven.

claims.event: Early in Zhenguang Chounu's mother had Diwan strangled.

claims.statement: Chounu's mother sent men to strangle Diwan early in Zhenguang.

claims.event: Fushengmou, of the Wuyin clan, was Diwan's husband and later received a noble title from Chounu. No year is given.
Early in Zhenguang Li Julie, titled Mohequfen, was sent to strangle Diwan. The English splits the title as Fen.
Early in Zhenguang Azhiluo raided Chounu, who was then defeated.
Early in Zhenguang Anagui fled south with his brother Yijulü.
Early in Zhenguang Shifa, titled Yifulü, defeated Anagui and killed Lady Hou and two younger brothers.
In the ninth month Anagui approached the capital and was received.
In the tenth month Anagui was seated in Xianyang Hall and, shortly afterward, enfeoffed.
In the twelfth month the court debated Anagui's return. That month may enter 521.
In the first month of year 2 Anagui and fifty-four others took leave.
In the seventh month of year 2 Anagui asked again for troops.

claims.statement: He asks that his senior cousin, who outranked the two uncles in the north, be seated in the hall.

His line comes from Great Wei. The ancestors lived on the northern steppe. The Gaoche rebellion delayed their homage. After his brother became ruler they sent Gong Guli. Treacherous ministers killed that brother and set Anagui up. About ten days later he fled to Wei.

His aged mother is still in the north and the people have scattered. He begs an army to punish the rebels. If his mother lives he would see her; if she is dead he would avenge her. He promises seasonal tribute.
Yuan Tuishe and Hun Hezhan report chaos on the steppe. He again asks for ten thousand troops.

claims.event: In the ninth month Emperor Suzong sent Lu Xidao and Meng Wei to welcome Anagui. The English Xiaozong is not the reading of 肅宗.
In the tenth month Suzong held court in Xianyang Hall and questioned Anagui.
In the first month of year 2 Suzong received Anagui's party in the West Hall and gave the gifts.
In the second month Suzong sent Dieyun Juren to Boluomen.
In the eighth month Suzong sent Wang Zunye to comfort Anagui.

claims.statement: He says he already knows Anagui's origins and tells him to speak fully.

claims.event: In the ninth month Lu Xidao was chief envoy to welcome Anagui.
In the ninth month Meng Wei was deputy envoy to welcome Anagui.
In the ninth month Prince Ji of Jingzhao, Duke of the Realm, met Anagui at Beizhong.
In the ninth month Cui Guang feasted Anagui in the suburbs.
In year 2 Cui Guang was ordered to see Anagui off beyond the suburbs.
In the ninth month Yuan Zuan feasted Anagui in the suburbs.
In year 2 Yuan Zuan saw Anagui off with Cui Guang.
At the tenth-month audience Anagui's younger brother was seated below the officials, then below the cousin.
Anagui's senior cousin was seated below the younger brother and above the two uncles.
Cao Daoxuan conveyed Suzong's greetings to Anagui at the tenth-month audience.
Chang Jing asked Anagui what he wished to say and presented his memorial.
Anagui says his elder brother had become ruler, sent envoys, and was killed about ten days before the flight.

claims.statement: Treacherous ministers killed Anagui's elder brother and set Anagui on the throne, about ten days before he fled.

claims.event: Anagui says that after his brother took the throne they sent Gong Gulü to Wei. No year is given in this speech. 顧禮 is Guli; the English Gulü is repaired.
Anagui recalls the day Cao Daozhi went north as envoy. No year is given. A note says Cao Dao is probably a shortened form.

claims.statement: The speech writes 曹道芝. The collation note says another text reads Cao Dao and that zhi may be an addition, while juan 75 often has Cao Dao without zhi.

claims.event: At the audience Anagui says his aged mother is still in the north, ten thousand li away, and that she may be alive or dead.
Between the twelfth-month debate and the year-2 farewell, Yuan Cha took Anagui's bribe and let him return north.
In the first month of year 2 Mu Bi conveyed Suzong's parting regards.
After Anagui fled, Boluomen defeated Shifa, was made khan, and later led ten tribes to surrender at Liangzhou.
In the second month of year 2 Boluomen received Juren with arrogance and sent officers to meet Anagui.
After Anagui fled, Shifa was defeated by Boluomen, fled to the Didouyu, and was killed.

claims.statement: Shifa fled to the Didouyu and was killed by them.

claims.event: Before the second-month mission, Yang Jun memorialized that the new khan was Anagui's cousin and that a large escort was required.

claims.statement: The steppe has a new khan, Anagui's cousin. They will not welcome the younger brother of a slain kinsman without a large escort.

claims.event: In the second month Dieyun Juren, a former envoy to the Rouran, was sent to Boluomen and refused to bow.
In the fifth month Juren returned to the fort and reported the situation.
In the second month Boluomen sent a Mohequfen among six officers and two thousand men to meet Anagui.
In the second month Qiushengtou, titled yijin, was sent with the Mohequfen and four other men to meet Anagui.
On the twenty-sixth of the seventh month Yuan Tuishe reached the fort and reported disorder on the steppe.
Hun Hezhan arrived with Yuan Tuishe on the twenty-sixth of the seventh month.
In the eighth month Wang Zunye was sent by relay to comfort Anagui and confirm his gifts.
In the ninth month Sinifa, the later Rouran ruler and Anagui's elder brother, fled to Huaishuo and asked for an army and for Anagui.
Sinifa reached Luoyang and Suzong received him in the West Hall, after the fourth-year raid and before the fifth-year obituary.
In the tenth month the court proposed to settle Anagui at western Turuoqi Spring.
In the twelfth month of year 3 Anagui was granted ten thousand shi of seed grain. That month may enter 523.
In year 4 famine drove Anagui's people to raid. He seized Yuan Fu, then released him.

claims.event: In the tenth month Li Chong joined the memorial.
In year 4 Li Chong led one hundred thousand cavalry to Hanhai and returned without overtaking Anagui.

claims.event: In the tenth month Yuan Yanming, Prince of Anfeng, joined the memorial.

claims.event: Suzong approved the memorial.
In the twelfth month Suzong sent Yuan Hongchao to settle Boluomen. That month may enter 522.
In year 4 Suzong sent Yuan Fu to Anagui and then ordered Li Chong to pursue him.
Suzong received Sinifa in the West Hall.
In year 5 the throne granted Boluomen posthumous offices.
The memorial proposed to settle Boluomen at Western Sea Commandery.
In the twelfth month Yuan Hongchao was sent to install Boluomen at Dunhuang.
Boluomen then plotted to join the Hephthalites and was captured. No tighter date is given before his death in year 5.
In year 5 Boluomen died at the hostel south of the Luo.

claims.statement: Boluomen died in year 5 at the southern hostel in Luoyang.

claims.event: In the twelfth month Yuan Hongchao went to Dunhuang to install Boluomen.
When Boluomen tried to defect, the Hephthalite king's three wives were all Boluomen's sisters.
In year 4 Yuan Fu was sent to admonish Anagui, was seized, and was later released.
That year Poliuhan Baleng of Woye Fort rebelled and the garrisons answered. The year is not numbered here; Xiaochang 1 follows.
In the spring of Xiaochang 1 Anagui attacked Poliuhan Baleng and was rewarded.
In the fourth month Feng Jun brought him further gifts.
In the tenth month he sent Yujiulü Mi'e with tribute.
In the fourth month of year 3 he sent Gong Fengjing. Suzong praised him and told him to stay put.
At the start of Jianyi, Xiaozhuang exempted Anagui from naming himself and from calling himself subject.
In the sixth month of Taichang 1 he asked a princess for his eldest son.
In the fourth month of Yongxi 2 the Deposed Emperor granted Princess Langya, but the marriage never took place.
After the emperor entered the passes, Anagui requested a marriage and received Princess Lanling. He later offered his daughter to King Xianwu.
In Xiaochang 1 Suzong sent Dieyun Juren to reward Anagui.
In the fourth month he sent Feng Jun.
In year 3 he instructed Anagui's envoys to keep the peace beside Erzhu Rong and to postpone an eastern campaign.

claims.statement: The Rouran khan has been loyal. He is camped beside Erzhu Rong and must forbid plunder. His offer to march east must wait, because summer does not suit the Rouran.

claims.event: In Xiaochang 1 Dieyun Juren brought gifts to Anagui.

claims.event: In the fourth month Feng Jun was sent to comfort Anagui.
In the tenth month Yujiulü Mi'e brought Anagui's tribute.
In the fourth month of year 3 Gong Fengjing brought tribute and heard Suzong's edict.
In year 3 Anagui was camped next to Erzhu Rong.
At the start of Jianyi Emperor Xiaozhuang granted Anagui exceptional rites.

claims.statement: Anagui has guarded the northern frontier. He need not have his personal name spoken at audience, nor call himself subject in memorials.

claims.event: In Taichang 1 Anagui asked that his eldest son marry a princess.
In Yongxi 2 Princess Langya was granted for that request, but the wedding did not happen.
In the sixth month of Taichang 1 Wujulan Shushifa brought tribute and the request for a princess.
In the fourth month of Yongxi 2 the Deposed Emperor granted Princess Langya, then entered the passes before the wedding.
Prince Hui of Fanyang's eldest daughter was Princess Langya.
In Yongxi 2 Princess Langya was granted to Anagui's eldest son, but the marriage did not take place.
After the Deposed Emperor entered the passes, King Xianwu persuaded Anagui and granted Princess Lanling. Emperor Jing later told him to accept Anagui's daughter.
The Prince of Changshan's younger sister was granted to Anagui as Princess Lanling.
King Xianwu granted Princess Le'an, renamed Princess Lanling, and Anagui received her with a thousand horses.
Yuan Shou was ordered to escort Princess Lanling north.
Emperor Jing ordered King Xianwu to accept Anagui's daughter. No year is given.
Anagui offered his beloved daughter to King Xianwu, and Emperor Jing told the king to accept her.
Yuwen Mohuai, a distant branch of the Southern Shanyu, ruled the eastern tribes and was killed by his people. No year is given.

claims.statement: Mohuai's tribesmen killed him for abusing the people.

claims.event: Pubo succeeded Mohuai and later died. No year is given.

claims.statement: Pubo died and his son Qiubuqin succeeded.

claims.event: Qiubuqin succeeded Pubo, married Emperor Pingwen's daughter, and died. No year is given.

claims.statement: Qiubuqin died and his son Mohui succeeded.

claims.event: Emperor Pingwen's daughter married Qiubuqin. No year is given.
Emperor Pingwen's unnamed daughter married Qiubuqin.
Mohui succeeded Qiubuqin, fought Murong Hui, proclaimed himself Shanyu, and died. No year is given. His birth name is suppressed.

claims.statement: Mohui died and his son Xunniyan succeeded.

claims.event: Mohui's original name violated the Founding Emperor's taboo. No year and no personal name are given.
Mohui sent his brother Quyun against Murong Hui, who defeated him. The English does not give Quyun's name in the idiomatic line; the Chinese does. No year.
Before Emperor Hui's third year Murong Hui defeated Quyun, Suyan, and Xunniyan.
In Emperor Hui's third year Murong Hui's son Ren killed Xibadui, and Hui then broke Qidedui.
Mohui sent Suyan of a detached force against Murong Hui at Jicheng and he was defeated. No year. The idiomatic English leaves his name out.
Xunniyan attacked Murong Hui, was captured by Han's ambush, then married Emperor Zhao's daughter. This is before his son's campaign in Emperor Hui's third year.

claims.statement: Xunniyan died before his son Qidedui's campaign in Emperor Hui's third year.
Han is the danger and should be taken before the city.

claims.event: Murong Han ambushed Xunniyan and burned his camp.

claims.statement: Men posing as Duan Mobo's envoys told Xunniyan to hurry and join an attack on Han. Han had arranged the ruse.

claims.event: Duan Mobo does not act here. Han's men pretend to be his envoys.
After the defeat, Emperor Zhao accepted Xunniyan's tribute and gave him a daughter.
Emperor Zhao gave his unnamed daughter to Xunniyan.
In Emperor Hui's third year Qidedui held Baoshui, sent Xibadui against Ren, and was then routed by Murong Hui.
Yidougui later killed Qidedui. No year is given for that death. A dried turtle at Pingguo was taken as an omen of his fall.

claims.statement: Yidougui killed Qidedui and made himself chief. No year is given.

claims.event: Emperor Hui's third year is the date of Qidedui's campaign. Read as Jin Huidi year 3 = 292.
In Emperor Hui's third year Xibadui attacked Ren at Bailin and was killed.

claims.statement: Ren killed Xibadui in Emperor Hui's third year.

claims.event: In Emperor Hui's third year Murong Ren killed Xibadui at Bailin.
In Jianguo 8 Murong Huang defeated Yidougui, killed She Yigan, and Yidougui fled to Goguryeo.
Yidougui killed Qidedui and sent Mohun against Murong Huang before the Jianguo 8 campaign. Those events have no year.
In Jianguo 8 Murong Huang defeated Yidougui and resettled more than five thousand tents at Changli.
Before Jianguo 8 Murong Huang defeated Mohun, who lost more than ten thousand men.
Mohun, Yidougui's chancellor, was routed by Murong Huang before the Jianguo 8 campaign.
In Jianguo 8 Murong Huang killed She Yigan, Yidougui's champion.

claims.statement: Murong Huang killed She Yigan in Jianguo 8.

claims.event: Jiuliujuan of the Tuohe, from Liaoxi, succeeded his father Wumuchen, besieged Shi Le, and died leaving a young son. No year is given.

claims.statement: The heading writes 就六眷. s0345 writes 就陸眷 for the same man, the son of Wumuchen.
Jiuliujuan died and his heir was still a child.

claims.event: Rilüjuan, Jiuliujuan's great-uncle, was enslaved by a Kuru officer, later grew powerful in Liaoxi, and died. No year is given.

claims.statement: Rilüjuan died and his younger brother Qizhen succeeded.
He prays that his master's wisdom and fortune pass into his own belly.

claims.event: The unnamed Kuru officer of the Yuyang Wuhuan bought Rilüjuan and later sent him to Liaoxi.
Qizhen succeeded Rilüjuan and died. No year is given.

claims.statement: Qizhen died and his son Wumuchen succeeded.

claims.event: Wumuchen held Liaoxi, served Jin, was made Duke of Liaoxi and great Shanyu under Emperor Mu, defeated Shi Le, and died. No year is given.

claims.statement: Wumuchen died and Jiuliujuan succeeded.

claims.event: Emperor Mu's reign is the setting of Wumuchen's enfeoffment. No year is given.
Wang Jun, inspector of Youzhou, memorialized for Wumuchen and sent him against Shi Le. No year is given.
Shi Le was defeated by Wumuchen, later captured Mobo and swore a father-son bond, then received Pidi's surrender and sent Shi Hu against Wenyang. No year is given.
Pidi attended Jiuliujuan's funeral, tried to seize the chieftainship, killed Liu Kun, fled to Leling, and submitted to Shi Le. No year is given.
Mobo was captured by Shi Le, later captured Pidi, styled himself inspector, and died. No year is given. His father is not named; 從弟 does not identify which uncle.

claims.statement: Mobo died and the people set up Huliao.
He will not face south to relieve himself because his sworn father is in the south.

claims.event: Jiuliujuan's heir was still a child at the funeral. No name and no year.
Liu Kun's heir Qun went to the funeral. Pidi later killed Liu Kun at a feast. No year is given.

claims.statement: Pidi seized Liu Kun at a feast and killed him.

claims.event: Liu Qun, Liu Kun's heir, was captured with Pidi by Mobo. No year is given.
Yulin is called Pidi's 從叔. Pidi planned to kill him and later fought him. No year is given.
Emperor Pingwen gathered cavalry against Pidi. The English calls him Daowu. No year is given.
Shi Le sent Shi Hu against Duan Wenyang. No year is given for that fight.
In Jianguo 1 Shi Hu attacked Huliao in Liaoxi.
Shi Hu defeated Duan Wenyang at Leling and captured him. No year is given.
Huliao was set up after Mobo and titled in Emperor Lie's time. No year is given for the titles.
In Jianguo 1 Shi Hu attacked Huliao. Huliao fled to Murong Huang and was killed.

claims.statement: Murong Huang killed Huliao in Jianguo 1.

claims.event: Emperor Lie's time is when Huliao and Yulan received titles. No year is given.
Yulan was titled with Huliao, fled to Shi Hu, and died. No year is given.

claims.statement: Yulan died and his son Kan succeeded.

claims.event: In Jianguo 1 Murong Huang killed Huliao, who had taken refuge with him.
Kan succeeded Yulan, occupied Qi during Ran Min's disorder, and was killed by Murong Jun. No year is given.

claims.statement: Murong Jun poisoned Kan's eyes and killed him, and pit-buried more than three thousand of his followers.

claims.event: Kan moved south during Ran Min's disorder. No year is given.
Murong Jun sent Xuangong against Kan and then killed Kan. No year is given.
Murong Jun's younger brother Xuangong captured Kan at Guanggu. No year is given.
Tradition says a Xiongnu Shanyu offered his two daughters to Heaven. No calendar year is given.

claims.statement: His daughters cannot be given to a man; they are offered to Heaven, and the rite is not finished.

claims.event: After three years the daughters' mother wanted to fetch them. No name and no calendar year.
The elder daughter warned her sister not to go down to the wolf. No name.

claims.statement: The wolf is a beast and will shame their parents.

claims.event: The younger daughter went down to the wolf and bore children whose line became a nation. No name and no calendar year.

claims.quantity: a line that became a nation

claims.statement: The wolf may be a divine being sent by Heaven.

claims.event: The Founding Emperor broke the Gaoche, hunted with them as beaters, favored Beihouli, and buried him. No year is given.
Prince Yi of Wei crushed seven fugitive Gaoche bands. No year is given.
Chilejian, mofu of the Zhilihe, brought nine hundred encampments to submit. The English splits the name and the clan. No year.
Fandoujian, mofu of the Jiepi, submitted with thirty encampments. No year.
After a defeat Shelun entered Gaoche land, was attacked by Beihouli, and then destroyed most of that force. No year.
Beihouli, chief of the Hulü, fled to Wei after Shelun's counterattack and was made Duke of Mengdu. No year.

claims.statement: Beihouli died and the Founding Emperor buried him with state rites.
Shelun is newly gathered, short of men and horses, and easy to attack.

claims.event: Beihouli's youngest son Hetang was made an inner attendant. No year.
General Yi Yu broke the Yuanhe and Wupin remnant clans. No year.
Emperor Taiwu settled the eastern Gaoche from Sini Po south of the desert. No year is given.
Anyuan led the cavalry to Sini Po. No year.
Changsun Han, minister of the masses, advised against the Sini Po attack. The English 'Works' is not 司徒. No year.

label.en: director of the masters of writing

claims.event: Liu Jie, director of the masters of writing, joined the remonstrance. The English 'Secretariat' is not 尚書. No year.
Under Emperor Wencheng the five Gaoche divisions sacrificed to Heaven. No year.
Xiaowen summoned the Gaoche for a southern campaign and they rebelled. No year is given for that campaign.
In Taihe 14 Xiaowen did not yet trust Afuzhiluo and sent Yu Ti, then Kezuhun Changsheng.
The Gaoche made Shuzhe of the Yuanhe their leader, rebelled, fled to the Rouran, and then submitted. No year.
Yuwen Fu pursued the rebel Gaoche and was defeated. No year.
Prince Ji of Jiangyang was sent against Shuzhe and first tried reassurance. No year.
In Taihe 11 Douluon raided the frontier, ignored Afuzhiluo, and was then repeatedly defeated.
In Taihe 11 Afuzhiluo rebelled west from Douluon and was hailed as Hou Lou Fule.
In Taihe 14 Afuzhiluo sent Hu merchant Yuezhe and then Bojie.
After Taihe 14 Afuzhiluo killed his eldest son for incest and a plot.

claims.statement: The Rouran are rebels against the Son of Heaven. He broke away and will attack them.

claims.event: In the Taihe 11 revolt Qiongqi was titled Houbei and ruled the south.
Later the Hephthalites killed Qiongqi and seized his son Mietu.

claims.statement: The Hephthalites killed Qiongqi after the Taihe 14 embassy. No tighter year.

claims.event: In Taihe 14 the Hu merchant Yuezhe brought Afuzhiluo's arrows and message. Hu is the merchant label, not a second surname.
In Taihe 14 Yu Ti went to inspect Afuzhiluo and returned with Bojie, then went again with Kezuhun Changsheng.
In Taihe 14 Bojie came to court with Yu Ti. 頡 is jie, not nian.
In Taihe 14 Kezuhun Changsheng was sent with Yu Ti to the Gaoche. The English splits the clan as Kedu Hun.
When the Hephthalites killed Qiongqi they seized Mietu and others.
Meng Wei settled Qiongqi's refugees at Gaoping Garrison.
Afuzhiluo's eldest son committed incest with another of his father's wives, plotted to kill him, and was killed.

claims.statement: Afuzhiluo killed his eldest son after the incest and the plot. No tighter year than after Taihe 14.

claims.event: Another wife of Afuzhiluo was taken by his eldest son. No name.
Afuzhiluo grew cruel and his people killed him. No year is given.

claims.statement: The Gaoche killed Afuzhiluo and set up Baliyan.

claims.event: Baliyan, a kinsman of Afuzhiluo, was set up and killed a year later when Mietu was brought back. No absolute year.

claims.statement: A year after Baliyan was set up, the tribesmen killed him and welcomed Mietu.

claims.event: Mietu was restored by the Hephthalites and exchanged embassies with Xuanwu. Those notices give no year.
Early in Xiaoming's reign Chounu captured Mietu, dragged him to death, and lacquered his skull.

claims.statement: Early in Xiaoming's reign Chounu dragged Mietu to death.

claims.event: Murong Tan took silks to Mietu. No year.
Xuanwu addressed Mietu, sent Meng Wei to Qu Jia, and received Futu's hair. No year is given.

claims.statement: Mietu's loyalty is praised. The Rouran, Hephthalites, and Tuyuhun meet through Gaochang. Gaochang has submitted. Blocking the emperor's envoys is unpardonable.

claims.event: Futu fought Mietu north of Lake Pulei, halted at Yiwu, and was killed. The English Futtu is repaired. No year.

claims.statement: Mietu killed Futu north of Lake Pulei and sent his hair to Meng Wei.

claims.event: King Qu Jia of Gaochang asked to move inward. No year.
Xuanwu sent Meng Wei to escort Qu Jia. At Yiwu the Rouran fled from his army, and Mietu sent him Futu's hair. No year.
Yu Liang was sent to answer Mietu's tribute. No year.
Mietu sent Chihezhen of the Wuyin, titled Mohequfen, with tribute. The English Fenwuyin Chizi Zhen splits the title, clan, and name. No year.
Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign Chounu killed Mietu.
Early in Xiaoming's reign Chounu captured and killed Mietu.
Some years after Mietu's death the Hephthalites let Yifu return. No year for that return.
During Zhengguang Yifu sent tribute and asked for a palanquin and insignia.

claims.statement: After a defeat by the Rouran, Yifu's brother Yueju killed him. No year is given.

claims.event: Gu Kai was sent to invest Yifu. No year.
Yifu defeated the Rouran and their khan Boluomen fled to Liangzhou. The English Brahmana treats the name as a common noun. No year.
Yueju killed Yifu and took the throne. No year is given for the killing.
During Tianping the Rouran defeated Yueju, and Bishi killed him.

claims.statement: During Tianping Bishi killed Yueju and took the throne.

claims.event: During Tianping Bishi killed Yueju and made himself king.
During Xinghe the Rouran defeated Bishi.
In the Xinghe narrative Qubin fled the Rouran and was made King of the Gaoche, then died of illness.

claims.statement: Qubin soon died of illness after his enfeoffment in the Xinghe narrative.

claims.event: Prince Xianwu of Qi had Qubin enfeoffed during the Xinghe narrative.
In Dengguo 3 Taizu broke the Jieru on the Nüshui.
The next spring he carried off their people and herds.
In Dengguo 5 he and Murong Lin broke the Hetulin and Hexi.
In the summer of year 8, still in the Dengguo narrative, he crushed the Houlülin and captured Yanguyan.
In Huangshi 2 the imperial carriage marched on Zhongshan. In this narrative that is Taizu.
Still in the Huangshi 2 narrative, Taizu sent Yu Yue against Ni Wuni.
Taizu received Taisifu of the Xuegan, ordered him to hand over Qubie, and marched against him when he refused. No year is given.
In Dengguo 5 Murong Lin joined Taizu and they broke the Hetulin.
In Dengguo 5 Hetulin chief Wudijian submitted.
In Dengguo 5 Hexi chief Kuhan submitted.
In Huangshi 2 Murong Bao attacked the camp at Baixi by night.
In Huangshi 2 Yuan Yan, governor of Bing, defeated the mutineers at Jinyang.
In the Huangshi 2 narrative Ni Wuni rebelled at Yinguan and Yu Yue destroyed him.

claims.statement: Yu Yue destroyed Ni Wuni and his allies in the Huangshi 2 narrative.

claims.event: Hexi chief Chinugen rebelled with Ni Wuni.

claims.statement: Yu Yue's destruction of Ni Wuni and the others includes Chinugen.

claims.event: Prince Yuan Shun of Nan'an failed against the rebels, and thousands died.
Yu Yue, Anyuan general, destroyed Ni Wuni and the others.
During Dengguo, Houlülin chief Chifa raided the Kushui, before the summer of year 8.
In the summer of year 8 Taizu captured sub-chief Yanguyan.
After Weichen's destruction his son Qubie fled to the Xuegan. The death itself is not narrated here.
Taisifu of the Xuegan submitted, sheltered Qubie, lost his family when the town was sacked, and fled to Yao Xing. No year.

claims.statement: Qubie came in extremity. He would rather die with him than hand him over.

claims.event: In Tianci 5 Qubie raided until the region west of Shang submitted.
Qubie, Weichen's son, later called Helian Qubie, sheltered with Taisifu and afterward destroyed the remaining Duolan. The Tongwan fall and that destruction have no year here.
Taisifu marched out to attack Cao Fuyin. No office and no year are given.
Taisifu fled to Yao Xing and soon returned north of the mountains. No year.
In Tianxing 4 Muyigan fled from Prince Zun at Gaoping.
Muyigan of the Duolan raided from Jincheng to Anding before the Tianxing 4 campaign. Those raids have no separate year.
In Tianxing 4 Prince Zun of Changshan was sent against Muyigan at Gaoping.
In Tianxing 5 He Tu led six thousand cavalry and captured the Chufu and Suguyan.
In the seventh month of Yongxing 5 Xi Jin was sent against the Yuele Beini and relocated them.
The historiographer's comment calls the splintered tribes of Wei and Jin heirs of Modu. No year of Modu's own life is given.

claims.statement: The comment recalls Modu as the stock from which later frontier peoples descended.

claims.event: The notes say Wei Shou's original Biography 91 is lost and quote him on the khaghan title Fumingdun. No year is given.

claims.statement: Fumingdun means constant in the Wei language.

claims.event: Taizu's annals record the Hetuolin in the fifth month of Dengguo 5.
The same annals record them in the twelfth month of Dengguo 5, which may fall in 391.
Taizu's annals record the Hetuolin in the second month of Huangshi 2.
A note says the main text has Taizu enfeoff Ba and Han together as Anyuan General and Marquis of Pingji, and suspects the title after Ba is missing. No year is given.
Hong's textual notes treat the character 蠱 as a form of 蟲. No year is given.

claims.statement: 蠱 is a form of the character 蟲.

claims.event: The note says Tuoba Tao deliberately used the slur Ruru for the people who called themselves Rouran. No year is given for that choice.
In the eighth month of Shenjia 1 Tuoba Tao made an eastern progress to Guangning and returned from there.

claims.statement: The idiomatic English drops 神䴥元年八月 and the literal writes Shenlu. The Chinese is Shenjia year 1, month 8.

claims.event: The main text, as quoted, has Taizu name Ba and Han together as Anyuan General and Marquis of Pingji. The note says two men cannot share the marquisate and that Qiba's own title is probably missing. No year.
Wu Han is the Han of the suspect joint enfeoffment with Qiba. No year, and the note does not assign the marquisate to him alone.
In the eighth month of Shenjia 1 Datan sent his son with more than ten thousand riders into the frontier.
Datan's unnamed son led more than ten thousand riders into the frontier in the eighth month of Shenjia 1.
Prince of Yueping, whose name the Tongjian gives as Pi, led fifteen generals on the western route. No year is given in this note.
Prince Na of Gaoliang took the eastern route, inherited that title, and is recorded leading troops in Shizu's annals. No year is stated.

claims.statement: Some editions and Beishi write 高昌 for 高涼. Tongjian and Na's biography read Gaoliang. Gaochang is the corruption.

claims.event: Na's biography is appended to that of Prince Gu of Gaoliang, whose title Na inherited. The note gives Gu no year and does not call Na his son.
The passage before this note treats Gaozong Tuoba Jun in Tai'an 4.
A khaghan title Fugudun is quoted, glossed by Wei Shou as meaning constant when read Fumingdun. This note does not name him or give a year.

claims.statement: The printed text has 伏古敦. Cefu and Tongjian read 名, and Hu Sanxing quotes Wei Shou's 'Fumingdun means constant.' The note suspects 古 is corrupt.

claims.event: Hu Sanxing's comment quotes Wei Shou on Fumingdun, and he and Sima Guang are said to have seen copies that read Ming. No year.

claims.statement: Wei Shou says Fumingdun means constant in the Wei language.

claims.event: Sima Guang's Wei Shu and Beishi copies are said to read Ming in the khaghan title. No year.
An envoy titled yijin, Weibijian, was sent to court. The note does not give a year.
Hu notes that yijin is a Rouran ministerial title. No year.

claims.statement: Yijin is a Rouran ministerial title.

claims.event: The note says the title yijin appears again with Qiushengtou. No year and no further event.
Futu married Douluon's wife, Lady Hou Lüling. The note gives no year. The English treats Douluon as Dougun.
The lemma calls the woman Douluon's wife. It does not narrate Douluon's death or give a year.
Lady Hou Lüling was Douluon's wife and was married by Futu. No year.
A stele of Yuan Hong mourning Prince Bi names Si Lü Ani on its reverse. No year is given.
Yuan Hong's stele mourns Prince Bi. The note gives no year for Bi himself; the stele is a later commemoration.

claims.statement: Yuan Hong's stele mourns Prince Bi and names Si Lü Ani on the reverse.

claims.event: Si Lü Ani is named on the reverse of Yuan Hong's stele to Prince Bi. No office and no year.
Cao Daozhi, also written Cao Dao, went north as an envoy. The note cannot confirm the character 芝 and gives no year.

claims.statement: The lemma has 曹道芝. The text above and Feng Yuanxing's biography have 曹道 with no 芝. The note leaves the extra character unresolved.

claims.event: Cao Dao is attached to Feng Yuanxing's biography in juan 75. No year.
A proposal says Anagui should be stationed at the Turuo-Xi spring. Tongjian lacks the character west. No year.
Before a marriage could take place, the emperor entered the Pass. The note does not name him or the bride and gives no year.
The biography says someone married a daughter of Emperor Pingwen. Qian says that woman was not the daughter of Yulü. No year.
The biography says she was a daughter of Emperor Pingwen and was married. Qian says Qiu Buqin married Emperor Chuo's daughter instead, and that this biography is wrong. No year.
Qian Daxin's Kaoyi says Qiu Buqin married Emperor Chuo's daughter, not Yulü's. No year for Qian.

claims.statement: Qiu Buqin married a daughter of Emperor Chuo of Ping, not a daughter of Emperor Yulü of Pingwen. This biography is wrong.

claims.event: Qian says Qiu Buqin married Emperor Chuo's daughter. The biography had called her Pingwen's daughter. No year.
Qian Daxin says Qiu Buqin married a daughter of Emperor Chuo, not of Yulü. No year.
Han heard of an event and, in another line, captured someone. Zhang Senkai doubts that the captive was Suniyan. No year.
Zhang Senkai says the capture line clashes with Suniyan later seeing someone and fleeing, so the captive was probably the vanguard. No year.

claims.statement: The line seems to make Suniyan a prisoner, but a later line has him stern and then fleeing. It was probably his vanguard that was captured.

claims.event: One line reads as if Suniyan was captured by Han. Zhang says that clashes with Suniyan later being stern and fleeing, and that the captive was the vanguard. No year.

claims.statement: Tongzhi's Yuwen Mohuai biography reads 敗, defeated, where this text reads 虜, captured. Zhang Senkai says the prisoner was the vanguard, not Suniyan.

claims.event: Tongzhi's biography of Yuwen Mohuai reads defeated rather than captured in this episode. No year.
The note identifies Emperor Mu in this passage as Tuoba Yilu. Wang Jun used the Duan clan in his time. No year is stated.

Wang Jun of You Province repeatedly used the Duan clan in Emperor Mu's time and was already dead in Western Jin. A bad reading made him governor under Eastern Jin's Emperor Mu more than thirty years later. No year is given.

claims.statement: The note says Wang Jun was already dead in Western Jin. It gives no year.

claims.event: The note says a supplementer turned the dead Wang Jun into a You governor under Eastern Jin's Emperor Mu more than thirty years later. That emperor's own year is not given.
Rilujuan was of Mobo's grandfather's generation. Jin Shu calls him the great-uncle whose grandson Liao, that is Hulu, later succeeded. No year.
The tribesmen installed Hulu. Jin Shu says that after Ya died, Liao, whom this note equates with Hulu, succeeded. No year.

claims.statement: This biography says Hulu was Rilujuan's younger brother. The note says 弟 should probably be 孫, grandson, matching the Jin Shu.

claims.event: Jin Shu says Mobo died and his younger brother Ya succeeded. The note says a brother of Rilujuan would be too senior to succeed Mobo. No year.

claims.statement: The Jin Shu biography of Duan Pidi says Mobo died and his younger brother Ya took the throne.

claims.event: When Mobo died, his younger brother Ya succeeded, and Ya later died. No year.

claims.statement: The Jin Shu says Ya died, after which the great-uncle's grandson Liao succeeded.

claims.event: The succession of Ya and Liao is quoted from the Jin Shu biography of Duan Pidi. No year for Pidi.
Inferred only because the Jin Shu calls Hulu, under the name Liao, the grandson of Rilujuan. No name, no year, and no separate act.
The note equates this biography's Jiulujuan with the Jin Shu's Jilujuan. It gives him no year and no kinship.
Taizu's annals mention the Yuanhe in the third month of Dengguo 3.
The note says Biaohe Shuzhe below is emended the same way as Yuanhe. No year and no office.
An edict of Shizong is quoted. Beishi calls him Xuanwu. The note gives no year and does not name the person addressed.
An edict ordered Dongchengzi Yu Liang to reply. No year.
Taizu's annals, Dengguo 2, month 4, day guiji, write the tribe with 叱 rather than 吐.
Taizu's annals for the twelfth month of Tianxing 4, which may enter 402, write Muyigan with 于.
Taizu's annals for the xinhai day in the twelfth month of Tianxing 5, which may enter 403, name a Yueqin mofu.
Wei Guzhen's biography also writes 叱 where this chapter prints 吐. No year is given for him.
Erzhu Tianguang's biography says Moqi Daoluo led followers west to Qiantun Mountain. The English writes Wanqidao Luo. No year.
Moqi Daoluo led his followers west to Qiantun Mountain. No year.
Zhou Shu juan 1, Emperor Wen's annals, is cited for Yuwen Dao beheading Houmochen Yue at Qiantun Mountain. No year.
Yuwen Dao's biography is appended to that of Hao, Duke Hui of Shao. No year, and no kinship is stated.
Yuwen Dao pursued and beheaded Houmochen Yue at Qiantun Mountain. No year.
Yuwen Dao beheaded Houmochen Yue at Qiantun Mountain. No year.

claims.statement: Yuwen Dao pursued Houmochen Yue and beheaded him at Qiantun Mountain. No year is given.

claims.event: Hu Sanxing cites Du You on the location of Qiantun Mountain. No year.

claims.statement: Du You says Qiantun Mountain is in Gaoping County of Yuanzhou.

claims.event: Du You, cited by Hu Sanxing, places Qiantun Mountain in Gaoping County, Yuanzhou, the modern Guyuan in Ningxia. No year.

claims.statement: Qiantun Mountain lies in Gaoping County, Yuanzhou.

claims.event: The twelfth month of Tianxing 4, which may enter 402, is where Taizu's annals write Muyigan with 于.
The note also describes Muyigan raiding west to Jincheng and east into Anding, without a separate year for the raids.

claims.statement: This chapter prints 木易干. Tongzhi and Taizu's annals read 于, and Liu Hu's biography and the Jin Shu life of Helian Bobo read 沒弈于.

claims.event: Liu Hu of Tiefu's biography writes Moyiyu for Muyigan. No year for Liu Hu.
The Jin Shu account of Helian Bobo agrees with Liu Hu in writing the name that this chapter prints 干. No year.
Taizong's annals, Yongxing 5, month 7, day jisi, write Qin rather than Le for the Yuele tribe.
On the xinhai day in the twelfth month of Tianxing 5, which may enter 403, Taizu's annals name a Yueqin mofu.

惠帝三年 read as Jin Huidi year 3 = 292. External.

建國元年 = 338, Dai Jianguo, external.
